submission.justification: Absorber-F3 with 5mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.12% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This represents a significant performance advantage over F2 (3.76% at 5mm) and F1 (5.11% at 5mm). The 5mm thickness is optimal for F3, confirmed by systematic scans from 2-10mm showing a broad minimum around 4.5-5.5mm. The 5mm dimension is also a standard manufacturing thickness and matches the baseline from the 2025 simulation study, providing continuity and validation. All three candidate materials are listed as viable options and described as machinable to required tolerances, compatible with the mechanical support design, and suitable for the application. F3's dense alloy composition with short radiation length provides superior shower containment and sampling, directly translating to the best energy resolution. This recommendation achieves the primary goal of best possible energy resolution while meeting all specified constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 at 5mm achieves 3.12% resolution, the best among all materials tested. Systematic scans show F3 outperforms F2 (3.76% at 5mm) and F1 (5.11% at 5mm) across all thicknesses.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate materials in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy with short radiation length.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: All three materials are presented as viable candidates in the project documentation, implying they have been pre-screened for compatibility with operational requirements including maintenance accessibility. No exclusions noted in documents.
The recommended 5mm thickness is well within the specified 2-10mm range and represents an optimal value based on simulation results.
